name: Gotcha
tiedFor: Generic shrimp on hard sand. The Bahamas default — if you only carry one, carry this.
look: Pink head, pearl body, tan craft fur wing — the bonefish standard

name: Gotcha — pink
tiedFor: The original. Pink wing over pearl body, bright bottoms.
look: Pink head, pearl body, tan wing

name: Gotcha — tan
tiedFor: Quieter version for bright light and pressured fish.
look: Tan head, orange body, tan wing

name: Crazy Charlie
tiedFor: Rides hook-point up over shallow sand; the fly every other bonefish fly argues with.
look: Vinyl rib body, calf tail wing, bead chain — original bonefish fly

name: Crazy Charlie — pink
tiedFor: Off-color water or low light, when they need to find it.

name: Veverka's Mantis Shrimp
tiedFor: Bigger mouthful over grass. The fly to show a fish that refused a small tan one.
look: Shellback mantis with forward mono eyes, barred legs, lead eyes — the bigger mouthful

name: Bonefish Bitters
tiedFor: Small crab and shrimp profile that lands soft — the skinny-water, spooky-fish answer.

name: Bonefish Bitters — chartreuse
tiedFor: Grass bottom where a tan fly disappears.

name: Squimp
tiedFor: Squid-shrimp hybrid profile; a good change-up when the Gotcha is being refused.

name: Strong Arm Merkin
tiedFor: Crab that drops to the bottom claws-up. The permit fly.

tiedFor: Heavy crab with trailing beads that kick up sand on the drop.

name: Tarpon Toad
tiedFor: Broad, slow-sinking profile that hangs in front of a moving fish.
look: Flat yarn body, rabbit strip tail, suspends in the column

tiedFor: Wide, translucent baitfish profile that holds shape in the water.

name: Walt's Worm — hot spot

name: Pheasant Tail — flashback

name: Perdigon

name: Perdigon — black
tiedFor: Silhouette in bright light or thin water.

name: Zebra Midge
tiedFor: Midge pupa. Two materials and a bead, and it outfishes far more complicated flies in winter.

name: Zebra Midge — black

name: Zebra Midge — red
tiedFor: Blood-midge larvae in silty, slow water.
